chunks: 1868 - He said: And I asked him about vomiting during the Month of Ramadan. He said:
"If it is something that overcomes him involuntarily, then there is no harm. But if it is something for which he compels himself, then he has broken the fast, and qada' is upon him."

key_terms.الْقَضَاءُ: making up the missed fast later
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, the time of obligatory fasting
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; no invalidation in this case
key_terms.يُكْرِهُ عَلَيْهِ نَفْسَهُ: he forces himself to do it

ai.seo_question: Does vomiting invalidate the fast in Ramadan according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about vomiting while fasting in Ramadan. Involuntary vomiting does not invalidate the fast, while deliberate self-induced vomiting breaks the fast and requires qada'.
